coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: About 5,118 retail stations in the FQMP database (June 2024). Petroleum Supply (Amendment) Act 2023 appears enacted (NOC monopoly on imports). Enforcement targets siting breaches (road reserves, canopy space, spacing), stations rebranding to dodge closure, and a 10% fuel-adulteration fine (UNBS/MEMD, March 2026). No Ugandan LPG distributor licensing rules found (searches returned Kenya EPRA only); LPG licensing details are unverified. Weak candidates only (C09).

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Warehouse Receipt System Act 2006 and 2007 Regulations: licensed public and private warehouses, keepers and inspectors, bonding and insurance. Current licensing and return duties, and UCDA buyer returns, could not be confirmed. Coffee EUDR is already K02/K06. One weak unverified candidate (C10).

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: SACCO returns are K04. Money lenders are licensed under the same Tier 4 Act 2016 (s.84), so they are a different buyer group (C06). The UMRA 2024 renewal notice gives no deadline or returns detail; the PDF behind it was not read.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: The National Health Insurance Scheme Bill has not become law: passed by Parliament in 2021, withdrawn, revised version awaiting Cabinet in 2025, being repackaged in April 2026. No state-scheme claims duty exists to build for yet. Nothing new; watch for NHIS enactment.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: The National Drug and Health Products Authority Bill 2025 would replace the NDP&A Act Cap 198. A June 2026 Ministry of Health letter says the NDA alone licenses drug outlets and the Allied Health Professionals Council must stop licensing drug shops; allied health professionals now need NDA premises approval. Import returns for narcotics are due within 30 days (2014 Regulations). A compliance study found only 49 of 100 pharmacies had a controlled-drugs book. Revive lead on K07 (C07).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security organisations need an IGP licence under the Police (Control of Private Security Organisations) rules 2013. Guards must be registered with Police before hire and renewed yearly. Police publish an annual list of licensed PSOs and gun dealers (2026 list issued March 2026). Police took over guard training in March 2026. The industry body TUPSA complains of heavy fees. Estimated 50,000-82,000 guards. Cleaning and manpower agencies: nothing found (C05).

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mining and Minerals Act 2022 (in force 13 Oct 2022) and Licensing Regulations 2023 create small-scale and artisanal licences. A mineral dealer licence is needed for any mineral, including construction minerals, via the MCRS portal. Returns and sand/quarry duties not confirmed. PAU National Suppliers Database (oil and gas suppliers): 1,752 registered entities in 2018, annual refresh; current status unknown. Candidates C03 and C11.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: FIA Online Registration Guidelines (Jan 2024): goAML is the only registration route. Second Schedule includes advocates, notaries and accountants; real estate agents not confirmed in the excerpt seen. Duties: MLCO, STRs and LCTRs on goAML, change notifications within 15 days. The FIA guidelines PDF returned a 503 when fetched. Candidate C08.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Uganda Tourism Act 2008 (ss.13-14) and Registration and Licensing of Tourist Accommodation Regulations 2014. Annual operating licence (about UGX 200,000, fee unconfirmed). UTB began closing unlicensed facilities on 18 Nov 2024 with Police; 20 sealed. No guest-register or levy duty found. No 'Tourism Act 2022' exists. Candidate C04 (weak).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Fish: Department of Fisheries Resources is the competent authority; exporters must be HACCP-compliant (only about 9 established processors), so the buyer base is too small. Timber export needs a forestry licence (NFTPA s.44); illegal timber and DRC trade is a live issue but no registry or software hook found. Coffee is K02/K06. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 31. Occupational Safety and Health (Amendment) Act 2025: all workplaces
coverage.found: Act No. 20 of 2025, in force 25 July 2025, removes the 20-employee threshold. Duties: safety committees and officers, workplace health surveillance plan approved by the Commissioner, notification of accidents and disease outbreaks (s.20A), risk assessments, annual audits (s.46), medicals, certified operator training. Regulations are not yet enacted. Workplace registration with the Commissioner already exists (C01).

coverage.category: 32. Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019: PDPO registration and annual compliance report
coverage.found: Every data collector, controller and processor must register and renew yearly (renewal fee about UGX 100,000 per a 2025 summary). Enforcement from Dec 2022; Google was ordered to register in 2025. Annual compliance report due about 90 days after financial year end (sources conflict). Offence: fine or up to 3 months in prison (C02).

coverage.category: 33. Betting, casinos and lotteries (National Lotteries and Gaming Regulatory Board)
coverage.found: Lotteries and Gaming Act: e-licensing, calendar-year licences, 2025 Responsible Gaming Directives, FIA MLCO and STR duties. MelBet licence withdrawn Jan 2026. A July 2026 five-year plan proposes tougher penalties. Betting-shop specifics come from vendor blogs only (C12).

coverage.category: 34. Insurance intermediaries (Insurance Regulatory Authority)
coverage.found: IRA list for 2026: 144 players, including 49 brokers, 33 loss adjusters or risk advisors and 22 bancassurance agents. A 'Regulatory Returns Forms' page exists but its contents and deadlines were not retrieved. Small buyer count (C13).

coverage.category: 35. Excise Digital Tax Stamps (URA)
coverage.found: More than 1,680 manufacturers and importers use DTS (beer, spirits, wine, soda, water, cement, tobacco, others). URA's 2026/27 risk list flags mismatches between stamps and declared output or sales; government expects an extra UGX 267b. Manufacturers complain about stamp cost. SICPA is the operator (C14).

coverage.category: 36. Money lenders under the Tier 4 Microfinance Institutions and Money Lenders Act 2016
coverage.found: Section 84 prohibits unlicensed lending. UMRA publishes annual renewal notices for SACCOs, moneylenders and NDMFIs and has announced enforcement against unlicensed lenders. The prescribed interest cap is 2.8% (UMRA FAQ, date unknown). Count of licensed lenders not found (C06).

coverage.category: 37. Environmental audits and compliance (NEMA)
coverage.found: FY2025/26: NEMA reviewed 2,086 audit documents, issued 283 improvement notices, ran 188 enforcement operations and 208 criminal cases (Ministerial Policy Statement 2026/27). Nothing on sand mining, brick-making or small-business permits specifically (C15).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper licence or registration scheme found. Legal basis is the Animal Diseases (Control of Bee Diseases) Rules 2004 (SI 73/2004): beekeepers and sellers of bees or bee products must keep production records for the Commissioner and file annual returns (tradebarriers.org/ntm/measures/view/4316, secondary summary). Rule 18 requires honey producers, sellers and exporters to meet UNBS/Codex quality standards. The UNBS table-honey standard DUS DEAS 36-1:2019 was a draft at WTO notification, and its final status is unchecked. Uganda has been EU-listed for honey since about 2005 via a MAAIF national residue monitoring plan. EU rules now (Reg. 2023/2652) require each exporting establishment to be listed in TRACES by the competent authority, since 29 Nov 2024. From 3 Sep 2026, countries must also appear in the Annex to Reg. 2024/2598. I could not confirm Uganda's status in that annex or its current establishment list. Reports (Monitor, undated and 2018) say exports are far below the 200 t/yr EU opportunity because of costs, certificates and buyer requirements, and that most honey is uncertified. TUNADO (apex body, about 100,000 farmers, 23 trained honey inspectors) exists. Digital tools seen are donor-linked pilots (Farmerlink, Sevi, Kucheza) and a Makerere hive-monitoring app thesis. The buyer pool for an EU-compliance product is tiny and exports are minimal, and nothing in the 1.2M-beekeeper base shows willingness to pay. Nothing new beyond weak candidates below.

result.competitor: The free state portal OSHMIS (oshmis.mglsd.go.ug, cited in a ministry speech) handles online registration and certificates. Per a 2022 Monitor article, the ministry's online system also lets workplaces report problems. I found no commercial Ugandan OSH compliance software. The only local efforts are the UNCST-listed "OSH Tracking and Measurement System" (a prototype), Kashari Consults' digital OSH compliance system (in development, per VC4A) and a Makerere research prototype for construction. There are generic international apps such as OHS Assist. Local OSH consultancies are a likely service competitor (not checked).
result.duty: OSH Act Cap. 231 (2006): workplaces must register with the MGLSD Commissioner, and occupying one without a certificate is an offence. A law firm and a ministry speech (seen only as a search snippet; the PDF returned 404) say the certificate is renewable every 3 years. The OSH (Amendment) Act No. 20 of 2025, in force from 25 July 2025, extends the Act to all workplaces (the earlier 20-employee limit is repealed). Per search summaries it adds health surveillance plans submitted to the Commissioner and mandatory training or certification for machinery operators. Penalty amounts and safety committee thresholds were not reached, because the KTA alert PDF could not be decoded. No lift, boiler or pressure-vessel examination schedule was found.
result.market: Not confirmed. UBOS has published the 2019/20 Census of Business Establishments report, but I did not get its totals. The 2001/02 census listed about 160,000 or more fixed-premise establishments, mostly with fewer than 5 employees. The 2009/10 Uganda Business Inquiry put 96% of establishments in the informal economy. Since the 2025 amendment, all workplaces are in scope in principle, which is likely hundreds of thousands, but formal firms that can pay are a much smaller group. The number of registered workplaces was not found.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under the OSH Act (Cap. 231), anyone using premises as a workplace must register it with the MGLSD Commissioner, and doing so without a certificate is an offence. A ministry speech and a law firm say the certificate is renewable every 3 years. The OSH (Amendment) Act No. 20 of 2025 took effect on 25 July 2025 and removed the 20-employee threshold, so all workplaces are now covered. However, registration itself is filed through the free state portal OSHMIS (oshmis.mglsd.go.ug), so the software would be selling only the record-keeping and amendment compliance pack. I found no commercial Ugandan OSH software, only a UNCST prototype and Kashari Consults (in development). Weaknesses: most firms are informal, enforcement looks weak, willingness to pay is low, and no lift or boiler inspection schedule was confirmed.
